problem: Embodied navigation benchmarks assume the agent enters a completely unknown scene each episode. Methods that use a pre-built map assume it matches the current environment exactly, so neither setting handles environments that change over time.
motivation: Real robots stay in the same place for long periods, so they can reuse prior knowledge, but furniture and objects move and that knowledge becomes outdated. The agent must find where the old map is wrong, and no existing 3D dataset offers multiple layouts of the same scene to train or test this.
key_idea: Define the Spot the Difference task (recover the current occupancy layout from an outdated map within a fixed time budget), build a dataset of manipulated semantic occupancy maps, and train an Active-Neural-SLAM-style exploration agent whose global policy gets an extra reward for correctly changed map pixels.
insight: Coverage-only exploration wastes its budget on areas that did not change, whereas the difference reward steers the agent toward places likely to change. Difference reward alone (DR) is insufficient on MP3D, but combining it with coverage (CR+DR) is best on most pixel metrics even though it sees less area, e.g. Gibson: 82.1% seen vs CR 85.9%, yet IoU 23.1 vs 15.4. With oracle localization the gap to CR shrinks (Acc +1.1, IoU +0.1), suggesting part of the gain comes from trajectories that accumulate less pose error.
method: Task definition: the agent gets an outdated occupancy map M and a budget of T=1000 steps, and updates it online into M_t. It is scored by comparing the final map with the ground-truth current map M*.

Dataset creation: semantic occupancy maps (SOMs, 5cm cells) are built by projecting depth and semantic pixels top-down. Connected-component labeling isolates objects, and movable ones are deleted or relocated, giving 10 alternative layouts per floor (2490 maps from 249 MP3D floors, plus 13 Gibson floors for out-of-domain testing).

Mapper and pose estimator: a ResNet-18 + CNN RGB encoder and a projected depth map feed a U-Net that predicts an agent-centric occupancy/explored map, which is registered into the global map. A pose estimator fusing RGB, depth and local maps predicts the displacement (x,y,θ).

Hierarchical navigation policy: a global policy (CNN over a 240-way discretized map, sampled every N=25 steps) picks long-term goals. An A* planner produces local goals, and an RNN local policy outputs FORWARD 0.25m / TURN ±10°, rewarded for reducing distance to the local goal.

Difference reward: r_diff is the change in the number of map pixels matching M* between t-1 and t. The global reward is r_global = β1·r_exp + β2·r_diff, with r_exp a coverage or anticipation reward (β2=1e-2 for CR, 1e-1 for AR). Trained with PPO for about 6.5M frames.
Metrics: Seen[%], Acc., IoU on changed pixels (IoU+ for added objects, IoU- for removed ones), plus m-variants computed only on visited space.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (first 2 blocks, ImageNet-pretrained) + CNN + U-Net mapper, CNN pose estimator, CNN global policy, RNN local policy (trained with PPO)
setting.training_data: About 4.5M episodes on 58 MP3D train scans (2070 generated manipulated maps), trained for ~6.5M frames. Gibson is used only for out-of-domain evaluation.
setting.observation: 128x128 egocentric RGB-D plus an initial outdated occupancy map; estimated pose (or oracle pose in a second setup)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT 10° / TURN RIGHT 10°, with hierarchical global goals on a map
setting.privileged: The starting outdated map (part of the task). The oracle-localization setup also gives ground-truth pose. Semantic labels are used only to build the dataset, not by the agent.

numbers_note: The task is new and not in the canonical benchmark list, so entries use 'other:'. The 'split' values follow the paper's test/validation naming. Cumulative curves are figures only.
results: On MP3D test with estimated localization, CR+DR reaches Acc. 37.8 / IoU 22.7, versus CR 33.1 / 16.1 (+4.7 Acc., +6.6 IoU) and the off-the-shelf OccAnt 26.2 / 11.5. On Gibson, CR+DR gets IoU 23.1 vs CR 15.4. With oracle pose on Gibson, DR alone is best on most metrics.
limitations: Only geometric occupancy is used; semantic reasoning about which objects are likely to move is left to future work.
Changes are synthetic (2D map manipulation by deleting or relocating objects), not real re-scans; the agent only detects occupancy differences, not object identities.
Coverage-based agents still see more area, and a difference reward alone is not sufficient on the larger MP3D scenes.
